input: Write a tribute post for my company's anniversary

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The milestone number (1st, 5th, 25th, etc.) dramatically changes the tone, depth, and narrative arc of the post — a 1-year post feels different from a 50-year legacy piece.
Knowing the intended audience (customers, employees, investors, the general public) determines the voice, what to highlight, and what emotional notes to strike.
The platform where the post will live (LinkedIn, Instagram, internal newsletter, company blog) affects length, format, and whether visuals or hashtags matter.
Tone can range from heartfelt and emotional to proud and professional to fun and celebratory — getting this wrong makes the post feel off-brand.
A target word count or length limit shapes how much storytelling, history, and detail can realistically be included.
Understanding the post's primary goal — inspiration, gratitude, brand awareness, employee pride — determines what to emphasise and what to leave out.
Knowing what raw material exists (founding story, key milestones, notable achievements, quotes from leadership) determines how much the writer needs to invent vs. shape.

gold.taskTitle: Write a Company Anniversary Tribute Post
gold.taskDescription: Write a tribute post celebrating the company's anniversary to be shared publicly or internally.

questions.title: Which anniversary milestone is the company celebrating?
questions.description: Identify the specific year milestone (e.g., 1st, 10th, 25th, 50th) so the post can be calibrated in weight, nostalgia, and significance.

questions.title: Who is the primary audience for this post?
questions.description: Determine whether the post is directed at customers, employees, investors, or the general public, as this shapes voice and what to celebrate.

questions.title: Which platform will this post be published on?
questions.description: Identify the destination — LinkedIn, Instagram, internal newsletter, company blog, etc. — to match format, length norms, and style conventions.

questions.title: What tone should the post carry overall?
questions.description: Establish whether the post should feel heartfelt and emotional, proud and professional, light and celebratory, or some other register.

questions.title: Is there a target length or word count in mind?
questions.description: Set a length expectation so the post can be structured to fit — a 150-word caption is a very different task from a 600-word tribute article.

questions.title: What should readers feel or do after reading the post?
questions.description: Clarify the main goal — whether it is to inspire pride, express gratitude, raise brand awareness, or prompt engagement — so the right elements are emphasised.

questions.title: What key facts or moments should the post include?
questions.description: Gather available raw material such as the founding story, major milestones, notable achievements, team size growth, or leadership quotes to build the tribute from.
